dehydrated_text:
Love is patient, kind, not envious or boastful, not arrogant or rude. It does not insist on its own way, nor is it irritable or resentful. It does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices in the truth. Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things. Love never ends.

For we see now through a mirror dimly, but then face to face. Now I know only in part; then I shall know fully even as I am fully known. And now faith, hope, and love abide—these three—and the greatest of these is love.

We understand that Paul speaks of love as obedience. If you join the church, complete obedience to Jesus is required. Remember when we committed original sin, becoming slaves to the devil. When Jesus died, it was to ransom us from the devil, making us his slaves and obliging us to obey him completely. There is no argument or individuality; only full submission.

Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God. Nor does a perishable inherit the imperishable. We will be changed in an instant, at the last trumpet. For the trumpeter went sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed. This perishable body must put on immortality, and this mortal body put on immortality. When this happens, death is swallowed up in victory.

Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting? The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, my beloved, be steadfast, immovable; always striving in the works of the Lord because you know that in the Lord your labor is not vain.

This obedience guarantees access to heaven, eternal paradise. Be a hardworking slave for 40 or 50 years and then enjoy eternal paradise as Jesus promises. The defeat of death lies in this promise.

According to original belief, pursuing our divine spark leads us to heaven. However, after death, people might find they cannot truly go there because they are slaves. This system extracts energy while alive, with patriarchs being the real customers, forcing their children into it. This explains why the Catholic Church is the most powerful organization today.
